claim: The human subcortex is comprised of more than 450 individual nuclei which lie deep in the brain.
source: The human subcortex is comprised of more than 450 individual nuclei which lie deep in the brain.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the composition of the human subcortex, presented without specific supporting data or citation in the abstract.

claim: Only 7% of subcortical nuclei have been depicted in standard MRI atlases.
source: Due to their small size and close proximity, up until now only 7% have been depicted in standard MRI atlases.
evidence: This is a quantitative claim about the coverage of subcortical nuclei in MRI atlases, presented as established knowledge.

claim: The new MASSP algorithm has been tested on 17 prominent subcortical structures based on a large quantitative MRI dataset at 7 Tesla.
source: The new algorithm has been tested on 17 prominent subcortical structures based on a large quantitative MRI dataset at 7 Tesla.
evidence: This claim describes the methodology and scope of the study, which is supported by the data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Subcortical brain structures are often neglected in neuroimaging studies due to their small size, limited inter-regional contrast, and weak signal-to-noise ratio in functional imaging.
source: Subcortical brain structures are often neglected in neuroimaging studies due to their small size, limited inter-regional contrast, and weak signal-to-noise ratio in functional imaging (Forstmann et al., 2016; Johansen-Berg, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Small subcortical structures are prominent nodes in functional networks.
source: Yet, these small and diverse structures are prominent nodes in functional networks (Marquand et al., 2017; Ji et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Subcortical structures undergo pathological alterations already at early stages of neurodegenerative diseases.
source: and they undergo pathological alterations already at early stages of neurodegenerative diseases (Andersen et al., 2014; Koshiyama et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Deep brain stimulation surgery is a promising therapeutic option in later stages of Parkinson's disease and movement disorders, as well as refractory psychiatric illnesses.
source: Deep brain stimulation surgery, originally performed to reduce motor symptoms in essential tremors, is now a promising therapeutic option in later stages of Parkinson's disease and movement disorders, as well as refractory psychiatric illnesses in obsessive-compulsive disorder, anorexia, or depression (Forstmann et al., 2017; Mosley et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In modern humans, Neanderthal-inherited alleles were preferentially down-regulated in subcortical and cerebellar regions compared to other brain regions.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The size, shape, and location of subcortical brain regions changes with development and aging.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Experience-based plasticity continuously remodels myelin.
source: Experience-based plasticity continuously remodels myelin (Tardif et al., 2016; Hill et al., 2018; Turner, 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Iron and other magnetic substances accumulate with age or pathology.
source: iron and other magnetic substances accumulate with age or pathology (Andersen et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2018)

claim: Extensive work available from animal brain models does not translate in a straightforward way to human subcortical anatomy.

claim: Recent advances in anatomical MRI have started to reduce the gap in subcortical structure mapping, each mapping a few additional structures or sub-structures.
source: However, recent advances in anatomical MRI, combining multiple contrasts and/or quantitative MRI mapping and utilizing the higher resolution achievable with 7 Tesla (7T) and above have started to reduce the gap, each mapping a few additional structures or sub-structures, primarily the iron-rich substantia nigra, red nucleus and sub-thalamic nucleus (Keuken et al., 2013; Xiao et al., 2015; Visser et al., 2016a; Visser et al., 2016b; Wang et al., 2016; Makowski et al., 2018; Ewert et al., 2018; Iglesias et al., 2018; Pauli et al., 2018; Sitek et al., 2019).

claim: Previous efforts in subcortical mapping do not yet enable identification of many subcortical structures in individual subjects.

claim: Manual delineation requires extensive manual labor from highly trained experts which cannot be easily applied to large cohorts or clinical settings.

claim: MASSP follows a Bayesian multi-object approach similar in essence to previous efforts.

source: The main innovation of our approach is to explicitly estimate interfaces between subcortical structures based on a joint model derived from signed distance functions.

claim: MASSP has been trained to parcellate 17 structures: striatum, thalamus, lateral, 3rd and 4th ventricles, amygdala, globus pallidus internal and external segments, SN, STN, red nucleus, ventral tegmental area, fornix, internal capsule, periaqueductal gray, pedunculopontine nucleus, and claustrum.
source: The MASSP parcellation method presented here has been trained to parcellate the following 17 structures: striatum (Str), thalamus (Tha), lateral, 3rd and 4th ventricles (LV, 3V, 4V), amygdala (Amg), globus pallidus internal segment (GPi) and external segment (GPe), SN, STN, red nucleus (RN), ventral tegmental area (VTA), fornix (fx), internal capsule (ic), periaqueductal gray (PAG), pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN), and claustrum (Cl), see Figure 1.

claim: MASSP uses a data set of ten expert delineations as a basis for its modeling.
source: MASSP uses a data set of ten expert delineations as a basis for its modeling.

claim: From the delineations, an atlas of interfaces between structures, shape skeletons, and interface intensity histograms are generated.

claim: Dilated overlap is a better representative of performance than standard Dice overlap and indicates that conservative or inclusive versions of the subcortical regions can be obtained by eroding or dilating the estimated boundary by a single voxel.
source: We observed that dilated overlap, that is, the overlap of structures up to one voxel, provided a measure of accuracy largely independent of size, for automated or manual delineations. Imprecision in the range of one voxel in the boundary is to be expected due to partial voluming which impacts Dice overlap. The dilated overlap measure is a better representative of performance and indicates that conservative or inclusive versions of the subcortical regions can be obtained by eroding or dilating the estimated boundary by a single voxel.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the validation results and a recommendation based on the findings.
